name: Dappen Black Forest Tapp Tarock
description: Dappen is a complex trick-taking Tarock game for 6 or 7 players, traditional to the Upper Black Forest region of southwest Germany. It is played with Cego cards and features one player (the 'Dappener') playing alone against a team formed by all other participants, using a 12-card talon known as the 'Dapp'.

overview.description: Dappen is a complex trick-taking Tarock game for 6 or 7 players, traditional to the Upper Black Forest region of southwest Germany. It is played with Cego cards and features one player (the 'Dappener') playing alone against a team formed by all other participants, using a 12-card talon known as the 'Dapp'.

history.origins: Dappen originated in the early 19th century in the Upper Black Forest region of Germany. It remained a local oral tradition, undocumented by card game scholars outside the region until 2024.
timeline: Early 19th Century: Game emerges in the Upper Black Forest.
1800s-1900s: Traditional play continues in families and social clubs in southwest Germany.
20th Century: Related to other regional Tarock games like Cego and Dreierles.
2024: Formally documented and researched by card game historians.
history.cultural: It is a popular social and family game in specific villages of the Upper Black Forest, often played in tournaments since at least 2017.
history.evolution: Dappen is historically related to the Swiss game Troggu (played in Canton Wallis) and is one of the four genuine games played with Cego cards in the Baden region.

setup.players:
Minimum Players: 6
Maximum Players: 7
Optimal Players: 6 or 7
Partnerships: One vs. Team
setup.deck:
Type: Cego Tarot deck
Number of Cards: 54 (22 trumps/Tarocks, 32 suit cards)
Suits: French (Clubs, Spades, Hearts, Diamonds)
setup.dealing: A 12-card talon (Dapp) is dealt first (usually in two batches of 6). The remaining cards are dealt to the players (7 cards each for 6 players, 6 cards each for 7 players).
setup.equipment: 54 Cego cards, scoring chips or paper.

rules.objective: The lone player (Dappener) aims to win at least half of the total card points available (typically 40 or 41 points) by capturing tricks containing high-value cards.
rules.gameplay:
1. Bidding/Dapping: Players must 'dappen' if they hold high trumps (Gstieß, 21, or 20). If most pass, the second-to-last player must take the Dapp.
2. Talon usage: The lone player picks up the 12-card Dapp, adds it to their hand, and then discards 12 cards (scoring them for their team). 5-point cards cannot be discarded.
3. Trick-taking: The lone player leads the first trick. Players must follow suit. If unable, they must play a trump. If they have neither, they may play any card.
4. Winning: The highest trump wins the trick, or the highest card of the led suit if no trumps are played.
keyRules: Compulsory Dapping for high trump holders.
No obligation to win the trick (no 'overruff' rule).
One player plays against a cooperative team of all others.

strategy.basic: As the lone player, use the Dapp to strengthen your trump suit and eliminate short suits to allow ruffing.
strategy.intermediate: The team should coordinate (without speaking) to force the lone player to waste high trumps and to 'smear' high-value cards into team tricks.
strategy.advanced: Carefully track which trumps and high-value suit cards (Kings/Queens) have been played to determine when it is safe to lead high cards.
tips: Conserve your highest trumps (Gstieß, 21) for crucial tricks.
Discard weak cards that allow the team to lead through you.

variations.name: Furtwangen (Klausmann)
variations.description: Full rules with Solo and Dappen bidding, compulsory dappen, Ulti, gstiesieren, and full or half game scoring.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant rules differ by locality; engine overrides to be added when implementing this variant.

variations.name: Breitnau
variations.description: No compulsory dappen; if all pass the hand is thrown in. No Ulti or gstiesieren. Stupfen (push) over strecken. Payment: difference from 40 multiplied by contract factor then rounded up to next 10.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant rules differ by locality; engine overrides to be added when implementing this variant.

variations.name: Buchenbach
variations.description: Six players only. Extra bids: Ein Hannes (one king), Zwei Hannes (two kings), Geiß (trump 1). First three tricks: Gstieß, then 21, then 1 must be played by holder; others must play 1-point trumps if able.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant rules differ by locality; engine overrides to be added when implementing this variant.

scoring.description: Score by total card points captured in tricks by lone player versus team. Points in the Dapp count for the lone player unless they take no tricks.
scoring.winCondition: Lone player wins with at least half the pack points (40 or more in 6-player); opponents win with 39 or fewer.

synthesis.shortDescription: A regional Cego tarock game where one player takes the dapp and fights the rest of the table in trick play.
